title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Compute eight quotient bits per clock in a shared DIV/REM unit
motivation:
The baseline's 199.837 ns path crosses operand forwarding and the EX ALU.
The ALU computes signed and unsigned division and remainder combinationally.
A full-width divide is a plausible source of the 156-cell path. Its delay
limits the clock even when executing other instructions. A reference-ISS run
of the canonical ten-iteration binary retired 2,922,015 instructions between
the markers, including 93,960 multiplies and zero divides or remainders.

Capture the forwarded operand magnitudes on launch, then reuse eight

acceptance threshold and 8.17 MHz would deliver the projected 50% gain.

title: Move DIV and REM off the single-cycle execute path
motivation:
The baseline retires ten CoreMark iterations in 4,491,485 cycles at a median
5.442 MHz. Gowin reports a 199.837 ns path through forwarding and the EX ALU.
The ALU selects full-width combinational quotient and remainder results onto
the same bus that feeds the data address. These operators are the strongest
candidate for the reported depth of 156 cells. The RV32IM reference
interpreter ran 2,922,015 instructions between the canonical -O3 binary's
MMIO markers, including 93,960 MULs and zero DIV, DIVU, REM or REMU
instructions. The run produced all five expected CRCs.

hypothesis.motivation:
The baseline retires ten CoreMark iterations in 4,491,485 cycles at a median
5.442 MHz. Gowin reports a 199.837 ns path through forwarding and the EX ALU.
The ALU selects full-width combinational quotient and remainder results onto
the same bus that feeds the data address. These operators are the strongest
candidate for the reported depth of 156 cells. The RV32IM reference
interpreter ran 2,922,015 instructions between the canonical -O3 binary's
MMIO markers, including 93,960 MULs and zero DIV, DIVU, REM or REMU
instructions. The run produced all five expected CRCs.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give EX one shared, fixed-latency restoring divider. At issue, register the
magnitudes of the forwarded operands and the signs needed for the result.
Process six quotient bits per clock for six clocks using a 36-bit dividend
padded with four leading zeros. Each bit uses the borrow from a trial
subtraction to select the next remainder. After the sixth clock, select and
sign-correct the quotient or remainder for the ordinary EX/MEM result slot.
This bounds the divider feedback path to six subtract/select steps and
preserves single-cycle EX for integer ALU operations and all multiplies.
Only a valid divide or remainder holds younger instructions. Older operations
drain, and the completed result uses the existing forwarding and retirement
path. The instruction mix predicts zero divider stalls in the measured
loop. At the baseline cycle count, a median Fmax of 8.17 MHz would deliver
the projected 50% gain. Check both median Fmax and marker-to-marker cycles
because a change in stall-generator phase at entry can shift the cycle count.

title: Predict direct control flow with a displacement-biased agree predictor
motivation:
Fetch advances to PC+4 even at a hot loop backedge or a direct call. Because
IF/ID is combinational, a correct next-PC prediction saves one fetch opportunity
on a ready cycle. Backward loop branches and forward exit branches can share
the same counter constructively if it records agreement with their respective
displacement biases.

hypothesis.motivation:
Fetch advances to PC+4 even at a hot loop backedge or a direct call. Because
IF/ID is combinational, a correct next-PC prediction saves one fetch opportunity
on a ready cycle. Backward loop branches and forward exit branches can share
the same counter constructively if it records agreement with their respective
displacement biases.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict backward conditional branches taken and forward branches fall-through.
Use the high bit of a 256-entry table of two-bit saturating counters to invert
that prediction at sites that repeatedly disagree with the bias. Predict JAL
taken and leave JALR sequential until EX. Decode direct targets from the
current instruction, so aliases affect direction alone. On the prototype,
stalled CoreMark took 4,188,667 bracketed cycles versus 4,491,485 at baseline
and passed all five CRCs. Gowin reported 5.236, 5.528 and 5.528 MHz. The
median gives 13.20 iterations/s versus 12.12. The cycle improvement alone
gives 7.23% more iterations per cycle. The prototype used 16 additional
LUTRAMs and three additional flip-flops. It passed all 53 single-retire
fast formal checks.

Capture, hold and flush those three bits with the corresponding instruction under the existing ID/EX enables.

mismatch between chosen and resolved direction. Correct to PC+4 on a

title: Halve the serial trial depth of the six-clock divider with radix-4 digits
motivation:
Gowin reports a 29.194 ns path from divisor_q to remainder_q through the
champion's six serial trial subtractions. The eight-trial design reached
31.094 MHz and the six-trial champion reached 41.649 MHz. Both completed
ten CoreMark iterations in 4,491,485 bracketed cycles, with zero DIV/REM
instructions between the markers. Shortening this feedback path can raise
the clock for every instruction.

hypothesis.motivation:
Gowin reports a 29.194 ns path from divisor_q to remainder_q through the
champion's six serial trial subtractions. The eight-trial design reached
31.094 MHz and the six-trial champion reached 41.649 MHz. Both completed
ten CoreMark iterations in 4,491,485 bracketed cycles, with zero DIV/REM
instructions between the markers. Shortening this feedback path can raise
the clock for every instruction.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Compute two quotient bits per trial level. For each radix-4 digit, form
T = 4*R + the next two dividend bits. Subtract D, 2*D and 3*D from T in
parallel. Use the borrow bits to select the largest fitting multiple,
append its digit (0 through 3), and carry its residual to the next level.
Three such levels produce six bits per clock with three dependent
subtract/select delays. The existing request-to-valid latency is six clocks.

Use the first clock after issue to register 3*D and process the top two
dividend bits. Their value is at most three, so this first digit needs
only small-divisor cases. Use three radix-4 levels in each of the next
five clocks to process the remaining 30 bits. This keeps multiple
generation off both the forwarded-operand issue path and the digit chain.

At the observed cycle count, 50 MHz would deliver about 111 iterations/s.
The acceptance threshold is just over 43.56 MHz. Check the bracketed
cycle count and median Gowin Fmax separately. Selection and routing of
the three parallel residuals are the main uncertainty in the estimate.

pass T as the residual at every digit, including setup. Reuse the

title: Resolve six quotient bits with two radix-8 divider stages
motivation:
The champion's worst Gowin path runs from divisor_q to remainder_q through
six dependent trial subtractions. Eight trials per clock reached 31.094 MHz
and six reached 41.649 MHz. CoreMark executed zero DIV or REM instructions
in its 4,491,485 bracketed cycles, so the divider limits the clock even
when it contributes no stalls.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's worst Gowin path runs from divisor_q to remainder_q through
six dependent trial subtractions. Eight trials per clock reached 31.094 MHz
and six reached 41.649 MHz. CoreMark executed zero DIV or REM instructions
in its 4,491,485 bracketed cycles, so the divider limits the clock even
when it contributes no stalls.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the six iteration clocks and change the quotient-digit datapath.
On the first clock after issue, divide the dividend's top two bits by the
registered divisor magnitude D. Only D values 1, 2 and 3 can yield a
nonzero digit for a nonzero divisor. In parallel, register 3D, 5D and 7D
using shifts and adds or subtracts. The other multiples are wires or shifts.
On each of the next five clocks, compute two radix-8 digits in series.
Each digit appends three dividend bits to the remainder and tries the seven
nonzero divisor multiples in parallel. Borrow bits select the largest
multiple that fits and its already-computed difference. This produces all
32 quotient bits with two dependent subtract/select levels per feedback
cycle. The existing EX issue, result transfer and retirement schedule apply.

Predict the same bracketed cycle count and a median Fmax near 50 MHz,
giving about 111 CoreMark iterations/s. At that cycle count the acceptance
threshold is just above 43.56 MHz. Compare the measured cycles and median
Gowin Fmax with these predictions. Wide digit-selection muxes or the
single-cycle multiplier could limit the gain.

title: Predict direct branches and JAL in fetch on the six-step divider core
motivation:
The champion still fetches PC+4 after every branch. Its combinational IF/ID
boundary makes each correctly predicted taken transfer worth one fetch
opportunity. On the previous parent, the displacement-biased agree predictor
cut the ten-iteration CoreMark interval from 4,491,485 to 4,188,667 cycles.
The champion takes the same 4,491,485 cycles, and its reported critical path
runs from divisor_q to remainder_q inside the divider.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion still fetches PC+4 after every branch. Its combinational IF/ID
boundary makes each correctly predicted taken transfer worth one fetch
opportunity. On the previous parent, the displacement-biased agree predictor
cut the ten-iteration CoreMark interval from 4,491,485 to 4,188,667 cycles.
The champion takes the same 4,491,485 cycles, and its reported critical path
runs from divisor_q to remainder_q inside the divider.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply the measured 256-entry agree predictor to the champion. Predict a legal
backward branch taken and a forward branch sequential unless the site's
two-bit counter predicts disagreement with that bias. Predict direct JAL
taken. Use the fetched immediate for the target, so a table collision can
affect direction only. Resolve JALR in EX. On an accepted prediction, let
the successor enter ID/EX on the next ready cycle. Recover in EX on a
direction mismatch, using the architectural successor including trap handling.
A prototype on the champion reproduced 4,188,667 marker-to-marker cycles
with both stall generators active and all five canonical CRCs correct.
It passed all 53 single-retire fast formal checks and the five-ELF cosim
suite. A directed test also passed with a mispredicted branch held behind
a stalled load and instruction memory stalled on the correction cycle.
Gowin's three placement options gave 41.642, 42.217 and 42.217 MHz.
The table added 16 LUT-RAMs and the metadata added three flip-flops.
The median gives 100.79 iterations/s, 8.69% above the champion. At this
cycle count the 4.6% acceptance margin requires 40.63 MHz. The median
placement's worst path remains inside the divider. Placement option 0's
worst path passes through EX recovery and the younger instruction's hold
logic, making redirect fanout a timing risk in the final implementation.

title: Register multiply partial products at the EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
The single-cycle multiplier limited both Gowin placements that set the
champion's 46.838 MHz median. Its path includes operand forwarding, a
full-width product and EX result selection in one clock. A reference
interpreter trace of the ten timed iterations counted 93,960 MULs.
Only 35,640 were followed immediately by an instruction reading the

The champion's median Gowin placement reports a 20.569 ns arrival from

motivation: Gowin traces the champion's 74-cell critical path from quotient_q to remainder_q through two serial digit selections. CoreMark issues zero DIV/REM between the markers, so shortening this path benefits the entire timed loop. The fixed retirement bound matters even for these infrequent instructions. hypothesis.hypothesis:
Build a fixed-latency divider from a synchronous reciprocal ROM and a registered multiplier used twice. For dividend magnitude A and nonzero divisor magnitude D, normalize V = D << s into [2^31, 2^32). Use i = V >> 20 and x = the low 20 bits of V. A 2048-by-45-bit ROM returns the intercept C = floor(2^42/i) and slope S = ceil(2^34/i²). Round the residual up to t = ceil(x/32768). A six-by-thirteen-bit product gives R = C - ((t*S) << 3). This makes the interpolation term an integer and removes the fractional carry from its subtraction. The shared unsigned multiplier first forms A*R. Extract q0 by shifting this full product right by 62-s, then reuse the multiplier to form P = q0*D.

R is a lower bound on 2^62/V because the reciprocal curve is convex and rounding the slope and residual upward makes the subtracted term larger. For 4096 <= D < 131072, s >= 15, so x is already a multiple of 32768. The curvature and coefficient rounding errors total less than 770 reciprocal units and A/2^(62-s) is below 1/2048. For D >= 131072 residual rounding adds at most 32768 units and the scale is below 1/65536. For D < 4096 the residual is zero, C has less than one unit of error, and D=1 is exact. Thus q0 is either the exact quotient or one short. Register A-D with its borrow early. On consume select q0+1 and A-D-P if A >= D and P <= A-D, otherwise q0 and A-P. Sign-correct the registered final magnitude for MEM.

motivation:
The champion takes 3,234,996 cycles at 85.328 MHz. Its ID stage calculates
five candidate addresses so an EX load can forward to the next instruction.

through ID to data memory. A scratch design with a registered external
request slot and local load service took 3,074,760 marker cycles with both
buses stalling and all five CRCs correct. Its median was only 72.449 MHz.

fed the hit decision back into EX admission.

motivation:
The champion runs ten iterations in 3,234,996 cycles at 85.328 MHz.

selects the next fetch address. Timing experiments that shorten just one
path expose the other. In a scratch design that moved dependent shifts
to MEM, the older rs2 select through the branch to ID/EX.pc limited the
median to 75.986 MHz. Duplicating fetch and decode for the two branch
outcomes also put a late selection on the data-address path.

motivation:
ADD and SUB produce their upper bits late in EX. A right shift can also
produce a low bit late because its input comes from anywhere above it in
the forwarded word. The result mux puts both paths through the same logic
before EX/MEM. The next memory address calculation is especially sensitive
to the delay of forwarded bits 12:0.

title: Fetch the unchosen branch successor alongside the predicted path
motivation:
The champion issues a ready EX redirect in the same cycle, but several
placements trace a long path from instruction selection through the register
file to the data address. Registering the fetched instruction gives decode
a full cycle. The cost is two lost issue slots when a conditional branch
changes direction. In a bracketed CoreMark trace, a 512-entry tagged
two-bit predictor model missed 39,683 conditional successors. Each such
branch has just two possible destinations, both known on a target-buffer hit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict one instruction stream and read one extra instruction on a
conditional branch. Use a 512-entry tagged branch target buffer with a
two-bit direction counter, and a 2,048-word instruction RAM tagged by
instruction address. On a BTB hit, fetch the predicted successor normally
and launch a synchronous read at the unchosen address using a second copy
of the instruction RAM. The alternate lookup needs only the saved target,
PC+4 and the predicted direction. Register its word, address and usable
bit with the branch as it passes through ID. Only the predicted stream
uses decode, the register file and the external instruction port.

At EX, use the actual forwarded branch operands. If the prediction misses,
annul the younger instruction entering EX. On a conditional direction miss,
put the saved alternate word at the INPUT of the normal IF/ID register.
If its full PC and valid tag match the architectural correction, decode it
in the next cycle while fetching its successor. Initially predict sequential
execution from this recovered word and validate that prediction in EX too.
This leaves one bubble on a covered miss. On a tag miss, BTB alias,
misaligned target or indirect target change, restart at the registered
architectural PC. Register target and linear match information independently
so that a forwarded branch comparison cannot drive a RAM lookup through
the correction mux in the same cycle. During ID, compare the alternate
row's complete tag and aligned address independently against fall-through
and the decoded direct target. Carry these two eligibility bits into EX.
Use the resolved direction to register a single alternate-hit bit at
the transfer edge. That bit authorizes recovery in the next cycle and
avoids a 32-bit equality comparator after the recovery-PC select.

In matched scratch cores with both buses stalled, retaining the alternate
word reduced ten iterations from 3,249,221 to 3,214,946 bracketed cycles.
Both runs produced all five expected CRCs and the validation banner.
In the ID-read prototype the recovery selector fed the register file and
address adder, reducing median Fmax to 57.102 MHz. Moving the read to
fetch and the word selection before IF/ID took 3,218,070 cycles, again
with the expected CRCs. Registering the fully checked alternate-hit bit
is the remaining timing hypothesis. At that cycle count acceptance
requires a three-placement median above 88.79 MHz.
